notes.title: Patch
notes.content: patch

notes.title: Parallax Effect Added
notes.content: Some platformer levels have newly designed foreground elements

notes.title: Minimap and New Level
notes.content: Rogue Randy now has a 2D platformer level, and a mini-map. Removed enemy combats from main level to make map traversal more enjoyable.

notes.title: New Levels and Boss Characters
notes.content: More bosses are scattered across the land! Each one has its own vulnerability, so experiment a bit see what you can find!

notes.title: New Levels and Boss Characters
notes.content:
Sorry guys that it has taken me so long to implement some new changes. Being in college has been quite an adventure!

Needless to say, I have learned a lot and am trying to implement what I have learned into this video game!
I hope that you guys enjoy what I have made so far if not let me know!

notes.title: Storyline Recreated
notes.content: Randy now has a crazy cool backstory! Collect glowing rocks to find out what happened. If you collect enough without dying then you will unlock a hidden ability!

notes.title: Different AI behaviours and holdable block
notes.content:
Randy's enemies now have a higher sense of awareness when fighting him. Most opponents that throw a projectile Randy's way will now run when he is too close.

Enemies that lunge or jump at Randy now have a much more controlled way of doing so.

Randy now has the ability to swing his sword more frequently without his torch being equipped!
Mash the melee button to unleash a frenzy!

Randy can now hold his blocking stance! Opponents that generate bleed damage still affect Randy, however, just so the pace of the game isn't bogged down by constantly blocking.
Press the Block button to see the results!

A light source also follows around Randy to help you see the distance that Randy can reach with his melee attack

There is a new item within the game that allows Randy to teleport from one part of a biome to another.
Gather up the green ooze from cacti or the really buff looking snails!

I will be uploading videos to give a preview of the mechanics as well if my explanations are not cutting it!

Lastly, since so many changes have been made to the game I have decided that I will be remaking some of the older trailer videos. Just a heads up as to why I am not making as many updates.

notes.title: Crafting System
notes.content:
Randy now has the uncanny ability to create items with the right ingredients. Traverse the world and find what you need to help yourself survive.

A smoke bomb can now be created as well.

Did you drop your torch and are too afraid to go back for it? Just make a new one!
Want to slow down your opponents and you aren't near any grass or cattails? Make a smoke bomb!

The crafting system can at the moment be navigated with the arrow keys or the mouse. I tried to accommodate multiple preferences.

notes.title: Inventory System Change
notes.content:
It took a while for me to figure this out but thanks to the indie game developing community on Youtube and a few Reddit pages I was able to readjust the inventory!

The new system that is in place now is configured with keyboard input. A mouse is no longer required unless pausing or dying in the game!

Thanks again guys and gals for bringing this to the forefront of issues I need to fix. If someone didn't address it I would have just left it as is. This would be a bummer because I feel like the game is so much more polished now and can't wait to hear back with what you have to say!

On a side note, I was not able to keep the dialogue items that I had in-game. I found through playtesting however that not a lot of people were looking for those. If enough people reach out however I will try my hardest to bring it back.

I plan to have an item that freezes time now that the inventory system doesn't do that anymore. I don't know how fancy I will get with the animation aspect but it could take a bit.

notes.title: New Stealth Mechanic/Item
notes.content:
Randy learned how to poison meat, to be honest this is a very specific skill, but nonetheless a fun little behavior.

Bait can now be used to reduce the health of enemies that eat it, or stumble over it.

The limitations are as follows:
1) You have to be hiding for enemies to take the bait if you are not hiding enemies will still try to attack you.
2) Once the bait item is picked up you have to press 'E' to place it on the ground.
3) Only one-piece of bait can be placed at a time. You can gather multiple pieces but only one can be present on the map.

There will also be a trailer video uploaded shortly after this post to help simplify the process.

notes.title: New Movement behaviour and increase on food meter
notes.content:
In efforts to fix this while still maintaining the graphic appeal that I am going for I decided to give Randy a little bit of wiggle room with the amount the map, he can see.

On the other hand, if your torch isn't equipped then your movement speed is reduced.

I have had a few people reach out to me personally about this issue and I want you to know that I am trying to make your voices heard while still keeping my vision for the game in-tact.

I also apologize for how long it has taken me to get these past initial updates through. I recently have been trying to get the inventory system I have in place to register keyboard input instead of a button press via mouse. With how I have the inventory system set up right now I just need to create an entirely new one from scratch is what it looks like.

All in all thanks for getting ahold of me especially in these troublesome times. Stay safe and let me know of any other concerns that you might have with the game.

notes.title: Map Separation, and New Torch Mechanic
notes.content:
The map of the game is separated into three distinct portions. There are little pink gems scattered about the map that can be used to unlock the specified areas.

The key for the starting room doesn't appear until the "tutorial" of the game is finished.

A torch mechanic was added so when the player gets hurt the torch doesn't fall every time.

The tall grass and cattails also cause certain enemies to move slower when they are passing through. I am trying to make the environment more of a tool instead of being just an empty space to run around in.

notes.title: New Song and Visual Effects
notes.content:
Made a new song to go with the game if the wind-effect audio gets stale.

The environment despite being super dark is now supersaturated with colors and the lighting of the environment has a glow effect added. 

Let me know what you guys think... I like it but if it is too much of a change I can dial it down a bit, or if everyone doesn't like it I can change it back.

notes.title: "Stealth" Mechanic
notes.content:
You can now hide in oddly-shaped boulders and ONLY only shaped boulders (at the moment).

Most creatures within the environment are careless enough to just let you pass by others are clever. It is up to you to figure out which are which.

The plan is to expand on this concept with other obstacles within the environment, so stay tuned.

Other audio effects were also added into the game to make it more IMMERSIVE!

notes.title: New Game Mechanics and More Sophisticated AI
notes.content:
You can now build barriers in areas where the locked doors used to be, but there is a catch! Sticks have to be picked up in order to build the barriers and it just so happens that giant chest carrying snails are the only animal in the game that is able to rustle some down.

Once the barrier is put into place creatures will try to knock it down so be careful of your surroundings.

A food bar is now incorporated into the game to make you feel a sense of urgency as you explore!

There is also a super cool potted plant that increases the size of your food bar/stomach because that is SUPER realistic!

A new animal is in the game that spawns oil Flasks which decreases how often you have to relight your torch.

I also decreased the lighting on the map for like the fifth time because the spookiest time of the season is coming soon and I feel like it adds to the importance of the torch.

notes.title: New Combat Mechanics
notes.content: Randy now has the ability to block attacks with his trusty dagger! Why is this important, why not just roll out of harm's way like the slippery eel you are? Because now every time that you drop your trusty torch it has a chance to go out! OOOOHHHH SO REALISTIC!

notes.title: Particle Effect Overhaul and Revive System
notes.content:
Hey, there folks I decided that these particle effects that I found out about really add a lot of extra value cosmetically speaking so I added more. A lot of the enemies will now generate an effect when hit.
 
I also created a respawn mechanic. Every time that you kill a certain amount of enemies you get an extra life.

The tutorial system also had a bug that took a while to figure out how to fix but I got it all situated now.

notes.title: Dust Effect
notes.content:
Hey there gang... I created a little particle effect that is activated when you take damage or roll.

I really think this little change adds a lot to the game aesthetically.

It's pretty cool I am very new to messing around with effects within Unity and am pretty excited to see where this goes.

notes.title: Rogue Randy is coming out soon on MOBILE DEVICES!
notes.content:
That's right Rogue Randy is going to be available on Google Play soon. The application right now is under review and will be available for 99 cents.

With that being said the price of this game is also going to have to drop because of the blood-pact I made with Steam.

This event is one of the main reasons why I have not been updating the game with new content as frequently in the past. 

I have been taking a good hard look at myself and my capabilities as a game maker and even with all of the progress, I don't think I can compete within the PC market as one individual. I am going to have to come back with a team of people to compartmentalize the work.

I've gotta say though it was tons of fun making this game.

notes.title: Cursor Issue
notes.content: Hey guys I made a boo-boo. I did not think that the graphic for the cursor would be different from any other sprite image as far as the rendering process goes. Apparently I was wrong. I fixed the issue as soon as I spotted it though so sorry about that.

notes.title: Changed input and readjusted UI elements
notes.content:
Hey guys and gals I changed the way that you can interact with items now. Instead of pressing the 'E' key you press 'I' instead. The 'Spacebar' is used to access the inventory. 

I tried to make the key configuration more streamlined and less messy. I am right-handed so for all you lefties out there lemme know what you think. I tried to pretend that I was left-handed and realized that the roll button is out of reach and am unsure what to configure the button to. 

I think the best option would probably be the right alt button but would like to configure it to something with more surface area.

notes.title: Updated Main Menu and created a new song tune
notes.content:
I made a guitar loop and slapped some reverb on it. I want to get some sort of percussion element added in to make it sound more accomplished later down the road.

The main menu screen animations don't actually look distorted now and on top of that, I created an entirely new sprite sheet to help deliver a hint at the dialogue/storyline that is implemented in the game.

notes.title: Created a new spawner type, and updated the lighting
notes.content:
For this game, the concept of environmental lighting is super important. That is why I went through all of the objects in my game and readjusted the lights that they emit.

The lights now have particular shapes and the brightness of the light dynamically changes.

I also made a new item that spawns a health potion a certain amount of times when it is walked over.

I plan to make animations for the spawner in the future but didn't this time around because I am so excited to release this content!

The graphic for the health potion changed to something more appealing as well. I felt that it did not look too great so I made this other one instead.

Again as always let me know what you guys would like to see in this game your feedback really means a lot to me.

notes.title: Readjusted bleed damage mechanic
notes.content:
The new yellow powerup I added into the game did not reduce the bleed damage enough according to my super cool playtesting group. On top of that, the bleed damage effect did WAY too much and seemed to completely ramp the difficulty of the game.

I am really going for a game that has a moderate challenge but not to the point where it is so frustrating and completely unfair that there is really no point in playing in the first place because progression is non-existent.

Even though this is posted as a small bug fix I think it will do a lot for the game. Again as always lemme know what you guys think! Without your support, I would not be able to do this.

notes.title: Created a new power up!
notes.content:
Hey, fellow Randy-ans (just a Calculus pun inside of a videogame pun to show how much of a nerd I am!)

I just created a new pick up item that reduces the amount of damage that is done by characters that apply a bleed effect. Now when you defeat one of the frogs with a staff it will drop the new item! I also increased the amount of bleed damage that is taken by said characters to give the power up more of a use in the game.

I playtested this a little bit and seem to like the effect that it has in terms of the game's design. I also know all the ins and outs of the game so if this new implementation is unfair in any way lemme know!

I also fixed the menu UI bug that was in one of the previous versions... sorry about that by the way for those of you who experienced the issue.

notes.title: Updated Graphics
notes.content:
The ground sprites were officially updated. I have been putting this on the back-burner so to speak just because I felt that there would be bigger fish to fry... also so to speak :)

When traveling out to the snow biome area of the map the ground will look a lot more layered and pixelated. To be honest the texture does not fit with the rest of the other biome's ground tiles but I think its a good contrast.

The shrub that spawns the shadow characters also got a completely new revision graphically. The light that it emits no longer stays within the scene for a certain amount of time after the burning animation is finished.
I figured this would add more to the importance of keeping around the torch item instead of relying on the environment as much for light sources.

notes.title: Change in Play Style
notes.content:
Hey guys I created a little squirrel hut! This new item in the game allows you to defeat the enemy that it spawns to gather a health-boosting item! There is also not a cap on your HP so you could just in turn farm the heck out of this to help defeat the more difficult bosses. 

In theory, the game should overtime give you increasingly difficult enemies to fight to cause you to flee the new spawner's area. At least that is what happened when I playtested so if this doesn't work as planned for you or you think it is too game-breaking please let me know!

I also made the floating shadow character spawn a key along with the skeletons after dying. I figured this would bring a more dynamic approach to finding loot. Fewer keys have been placed around the map as a result.

notes.title: In-Game Tutorial System
notes.content: You no longer have to access a boring menu to figure out how to play the game. This was my attempt to have something like pressing buttons feel more interactive. This was also another feature that was brought up to me by the community! You guys are awesome without you I wouldn't be where I am at with this game!

notes.title: Conflicting UI elements
notes.content:
The slider components (health bar, melee, throw, and roll timer) that I implemented into the game were set to be interactable with user input. This was not my intention I did not know that Unity enabled this option by default, which is my bad I should have known.

The value of the slider components changed according to the player's horizontal movement whenever an inventory item was pressed (when an interactable object was clicked on).

Long story short I disabled this feature with the timers and health bar and after playtesting a solid half an hour (just to be safe) the feature is now gone!


I also got rid of the remove button in the inventory there did not seem to be a use for it. If you folks want that feature back though let me know!

notes.title: Bug Fix AGAIN!
notes.content:
Hey guys it is Jake AGAIN! I was trying to implement this new UI idea last night and accidentally called the same line of code twice causing the Throw refresh rate bar to be degenerating half as fast as it should have! Luckily I caught this pretty quickly so I apologize I was just so eager to toss this feature at you.

With that being said thanks for all of the support! I made this game as a passion project and now I am just glad I get to bring it to life and share it with you!

notes.title: Bug Fixes And New UI
notes.content:
Hey there ladies and gents! I was playtesting the game a couple of days ago and noticed that there was a bit of a bug with the falling prone mechanic. I found out that the script was just using some garbage code and I am pretty confident in saying that it is completely fixed now! Let me know what you guys think I am super ecstatic to hear some feedback!

I also added in a UI system that shows how long you have until an action can be performed again (melee, rolling, and throwing). I will not mention the person by name just for the sake of privacy but one of you guys reached out to me and expressed their concern about not having this within the game, so here you go! 

If you have any questions or concerns please let me know! I want to give you guys the best quality game I can while still maintaining the central theme in mind!
